segments.text: Hi, my name is Risa Martinez. I work for USS.
So last time, Jeff talked a little bit about COS Unix and Sixplex.
So now I'm going to be talking about how they kind of both work together.
So in COS Unix,
you have access to the entire file system hierarchy.
And the way this is done is that once your file system is mounted,
an owning LPAR is assigned.
So once this is mounted,
now all the LPARs and users have access to this file.
And this is kind of done in two ways.
One way is that through COS Unix,
we forward all the transactions and requests associated with one file
to the owning LPAR.
And another way is called Sixplex Aware.
This is also called as Read Write Share.
In this case, the files are mounted locally to your LPAR.
And instead of forwarding, they're handled within that.
The reasons why someone might choose one over the other
could be performance or convenience, or it could be just by choice.
And overall, just the share file system environment has a lot of advantages,
such as your COS Unix data, it's always available regardless.
So even if your owning LPAR were to come down for one or the other reason,
your COS Unix data is still available for you to use from other systems.
This is just a brief explanation how this works,
but if you're curious and want to find out more about all the details,
there's tons of the commutation online you can go and read.
And that's all I had to share.
Hopefully this was useful.
Again, my name is Lisa Martinez.
